title: Dockway: Contextual Docking Panel & Cost Lens — Console IA Prototype
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and prototype a new Console information architecture pattern ("Dockway") that surfaces contextual actions, fast workspace switching, and an integrated Cost Lens for per-route token/cost visibility. The goal is to reduce navigation noise in large tenant consoles, make rollouts and model pinning discoverable, and provide a single compact surface for quick actions and cost-aware decisions.
rationale: Current sidebar and global nav patterns are overcrowded for power users managing multiple models and rollouts. Teams are requesting a compact, contextual surface that adapts to the active workspace and highlights cost-impacting routes. Dockway aims to be a lightweight docking panel that can expand to reveal rollout ribbons, cost breakdowns, and frequently-used actions without leaving the current context.
outcome_metrics: Reduce average click-path length to common tasks by 10%
Decrease time-to-switch-workspace for multi-tenant users by 25%
Increase visibility of per-route cost by surfacing cost delta for rollout changes (target 70% of users noticing)
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype (Figma + clickable flow) available and shared with PM/Eng
Usability test with >=8 engineers and product users showing at least 80% task completion for: pin model, start canary rollout, inspect cost delta
Dockway supports keyboard navigation and meets WCAG contrast ratio for visible elements
Design tokens and component variants documented and added to the design system board
Integration notes for Console engineers: APIs needed for route-level cost, rollout state, and workspace list
decisions: Use single-dock model (left-docked panel) instead of floating contextual menu to preserve vertical real estate
Primary entry points: global search, workspace header chevron, and keyboard shortcut 'g d'
Cost Lens will display estimated delta for model changes and a 7-day historical token trend
tradeoffs: Compact dock reduces surface area but requires progressive disclosure for advanced rollout controls
Bringing cost visibility to the dock risks noise; decided to surface only deltas and a secondary expanded view for full breakdown
usability_findings: Participants found 'Dockway' faster for pinning a model compared to current Settings path
Some users missed the hidden advanced rollout controls — added a sticky 'Expand' affordance
Users appreciated inline cost deltas, but asked for clearer unit labels and sample workload assumptions
review_feedback: PM (Miguel Santos): Prefer ribbon-style indicators for active canaries; ensure telemetry hooks for impressions
Eng (Lucas Nguyen): Need API contract for per-route cost and rollout state; initial implementation should be read-only to avoid coupling with rollout engine
Security (Priya Rao): Confirm audit events emitted for model pin/unpin actions
next_steps: Finalize Figma components and export tokens to design-system board
Sync with Servicing team on API contract for route_cost_estimate and rollout_preview endpoints (ENG sync by 2025-11-14)
Schedule moderated usability follow-up with 10+ console power users (target 2025-11-18)
Prepare engineering handoff doc that includes accessibility checklist and telemetry events
